glossary.definition: The designated operational role responsible for authoring, reviewing, executing decisions, and archiving records in a defined supplier quality workflow.
Documented information identifying external providers authorized to supply specified parts, materials, or outsourced processes based on verified qualification criteria.
A formal quality record issued to an external provider requiring root-cause investigation, containment, corrective action, and recurrence prevention evidence following a nonconformance.
A governance classification denoting software modules or functions—such as external supplier portals—that are scheduled or under evaluation rather than verified, production-ready capabilities.
Formal authorization granted by an authorized technical authority to accept and use externally provided material or components that do not conform to initial specifications.
A mandatory governance protocol requiring an authorized human owner to evaluate, validate, or reject automated or AI suggestions before commitment into a controlled quality record.

A classification structure that categorizes purchased parts or outsourced services into risk tiers based on the potential consequence of failure on end-product performance, user safety, and regulatory compliance.

A temporary, time- or lot-limited authorization that permits procurement from an external provider while outstanding qualification requirements or audit action items are finalized under enhanced controls.
A mandatory sequential checkpoint within a supplier onboarding workflow that halts progression until designated functional stakeholders complete and record their verified sign-offs.
A designated cross-functional operational body authorized to evaluate nonconforming product and establish formal disposition pathways including scrap, rework, vendor return, or technical concession.
A certified quality record issued by a raw material producer validating the specific chemical analysis, mechanical test results, and specification compliance of a delivered material heat or batch.
A quantitative evaluation tool compiling verified receiving inspection yields, PPM defect rates, delivery timeliness, and SCAR responsiveness into periodic supplier performance ratings.
A supervised governance tier applied to an external provider following quality or compliance slippage, imposing tightened inspection protocols and heightened managerial order approvals.
A controlled compilation of multi-year supplier evaluation records, audit reports, SCAR resolutions, and status authorizations assembled to demonstrate systematic control to external auditors.
An intensive operational support phase immediately following go-live during which systems and technical leads remain directly accessible on site to resolve procedural roadblocks and user issues.

reviewedChapters.title: Following supplier corrective actions: Supplier quality management software
reviewedChapters.summary: The guide chapter fully complies with the brief, contextual boundaries, and primary source claims. It systematically covers the four required phases of supplier corrective actions: triggering SCARs directly from receiving nonconformance records, capturing root-cause analysis and objective containment evidence, reviewing proposed corrective actions with human review over automated summaries, and verifying post-implementation effectiveness before formal closure. All APG external providers guidance claims and ICC Supplier Quality module notes—including the pending status of portal-based tasking and mandatory human review of AI summaries—are accurately represented and properly qualified. Each section contains required workflow parameters (role, input, decision, record, exception), concrete software evaluation criteria, and a clearly labeled hypothetical example. No unassigned FAQ section is present.
